title: Security Testbed for Preempting Attacks against Supercomputing Infrastructure
problem: Noisy attack attempts and unreliable alerts in supercomputing systems mask genuine attacks, causing permanent damages such as system integrity violations and data breaches. The challenge is distinguishing real attacks from false positives in high-volume alert streams at petascale HPC centers.
motivation: Preempting attacks before they compromise supercomputing systems is critical to maintain data integrity and prevent breaches at large-scale national computing facilities.
method: A security testbed embedded directly in live traffic at NCSA's supercomputer learns attack patterns from 200+ documented security incidents collected over two decades. Operators use a visualization tool to identify genuine threats amid the constant stream of false alarms. The system deploys statistical models (Factor Graphs, which map relationships between suspicious behaviors to calculate attack likelihood) to detect and preempt real-world ransomware families before they compromise the system in real-time.
key_novelty: Using statistical models (Factor Graphs) to automatically distinguish real attacks from false alarms in live supercomputer traffic and preempt ransomware before system compromise.
contributions: Characterization of unique attack patterns from 200+ real security incidents across two decades at NCSA
Interactive attack visualization tool for HPC security operators to identify real attacks amid alert noise
Demonstration of Factor Graph-Based models for real-time ransomware preemption at petascale supercomputers

metrics.other: Demonstrated preemption capability on real-world ransomware family
